correctness.rationale: The proof is a complete six-cell partition of the 216 strict profiles. Each cell has a direct six-order multiplicity calculation and an exact count. Independent replay checks all profiles with two serial-dictatorship implementations, TTC, and exhaustive coalition-based core computation; all four routes agree where applicable.

originality.rationale: The classical all-market RSD=CRE frequency theorem is treated as prior. The inspected primary literature contains the equivalence theorem and three-agent random-priority analysis, but not the complete five-spectrum classification, the exact profile counts 48/36/72/54/6, the six-cell structural criterion, or the exclusion of support size 5.
residual_risks: An unindexed exercise, lecture note, supplementary enumeration, or code artifact may contain the same three-agent spectrum table.
The 2019 broader RSD-equivalence paper had an inaccessible full-text endpoint during this run; only its accessible abstract was used for positive context, not for a whole-document absence claim.
The classification is specific to strict three-agent assignment and may change immediately with weak preferences or larger markets.

value.rationale: RSD is a canonical random-assignment mechanism and CRE is its classical market-based representation. The complete n=3 probability-shape classification identifies the exact first nontrivial lottery geometry, proves support size 5 cannot occur, and supplies a transparent profile criterion for every shape. This is a natural structural invariant useful for examples, verification, and comparison of random assignment mechanisms.
